title: Matched 2D, weakly 3D and finite-3D mean flows

definitions.U: Cell-centered Eulerian velocity averaged in the transverse y direction, converted from the saved Lagrangian field: U(x,z,t)=mean_y u_E(x,y,z,t). No temporal, ensemble, or x average in the field panels.
definitions.velocity_conversion: The cached Uc field is Lagrangian. Plots and CSV subtract the actual Stokes drift waves*S_reference*exp(2*k*z) to obtain Eulerian velocity. The no-wave controls subtract zero. Time differences are identical in the two conventions because the Stokes drift is steady.
definitions.profile: Horizontal mean mean_x U(x,z,t); x cells are uniform, so the arithmetic x mean is the horizontal-area mean.
definitions.change: The horizontally averaged current profile at t minus its own initial profile. Initial Eulerian current and q0 are not assumed zero.

roles.tiny: Weak 3D perturbation, initial transverse/2D eddy energy eta=1e-6
roles.finite: Finite 3D perturbation, initial transverse/2D eddy energy eta=1

definitions.initial_energy: Finite perturbations add initial energy. These plots do not compare equal-total-energy initial states.
definitions.coordinates: All saved cell centers are included, with no boundary exclusion, smoothing, or filtering. x=(i+1/2)Lx/Nx; z and dz are stored cache coordinates.
definitions.colour_scaling: Within each matched group, all three total-U panels share the exact data minimum and maximum; all three departures from the initial mean profile share a symmetric range reaching their largest absolute value. No quantile clipping. Colour ranges differ across groups and rows.
definitions.units: Plots use mm/s and m. CSV values use m/s, m and s.
definitions.scope: Finite-time 600 s individual realizations. Mean fields are derived arrays, not native three-dimensional snapshots. The smaller tiny100 amplitude is not plotted again; it belongs to the separate twin-amplitude test.
definitions.field_anomaly: The lower field row shows U(x,z,t_final)-mean_x U(x,z,0): departure from the initial horizontally averaged profile, retaining the present in-plane eddies and jets. It is not a subtraction of the initial x-z eddy pattern.
